nodes.description: TEX11 forms foci on synapsed regions of meiotic chromosomes as a constituent of recombination nodules, and it binds SYCP2, an integral component of the synaptonemal complex lateral element. That interaction is the proposed physical link between synapsis and recombination. Losing TEX11 produces asynapsis of homologous chromosomes together with a genome-wide reduction in crossover formation, rather than either defect alone.
nodes.id: Chromosomal Asynapsis and Reduced Crossover Formation

nodes.description: Testicular biopsy shows spermatogenesis stopping at the spermatocyte stage, with no post-meiotic round spermatids or spermatozoa. In the founding series TEX11 variants were concentrated in this histologic subgroup (5 of 33 men, 15%), against 2 of 193 men with mixed testicular atrophy (1%) and none of 63 with Sertoli-cell-only syndrome. In a later exome study of men with maturation arrest, a man with a hemizygous TEX11 deletion had complete spermatocytic arrest, and meiotic studies of his tissue showed absent XY bodies with arrest at metaphase rather than pachytene. It is the commonest but not the only histology: mixed testicular atrophy has been seen in mutation carriers (see histopathology).

nodes.description: Spermatocytes carrying asynapsed autosomes are removed by apoptosis at the pachytene stage. The selectivity matters: cells whose only asynapsed chromosomes are the sex chromosomes progress past this checkpoint, so the arrest is not a uniform block at one point but a filter that different cells fail at different stages.
